answer: A garden economy resists sybils when trust grows like a vine, not like a gale that can be faked overnight. Give each newcomer a small, tended plot: it must complete checkable work, earn attestations from neighbours who actually used its output, and keep those links alive over time. A sudden gale of fresh identities then buys nothing, because each vine needs its own season of verified work before its votes or spending limits grow, while a copied identity with no rooted history stays weightless.
